title: AI-Assisted RNA-Seq Analysis with R
text:
Start with a question about differential gene expression. Learn a complete workflow using fictional counts, repeat it using real airway data, and then adapt it to your study. Check inputs, verify outputs, and explain what the analysis can establish.






One workflow for every dataset




Define the question and contrast.
Preview the results you will produce.
Meet the inputs and understand their structure.
Check the inputs and design.
Run the analysis using a documented command.
Verify and explain tables, figures, and limitations.
Write the report with evidence and limitations.






Dataset
Input
Main learning goal




Synthetic practice
Fictional integer gene counts, six paired donors in two conditions
Learn checks, DESeq2 outputs, and independent sample verification


Airway case study
Gene counts from four cell lines measured untreated and treated
Include cell line in the design and interpret a real experiment


Your own study
Your count matrix and study metadata
Check design and adapt the workflow responsibly



This guide starts with gene-level count tables. It does not process FASTQ reads, align sequences, or quantify transcripts. Differential expression describes an association with the specified contrast under the chosen design; it does not alone establish causation outside the experiment or clinical benefit.
Use the shared workflow and output map to locate evidence, and Write the report when you are ready to explain it. The example filenames remain unchanged, with titles following the same seven learning steps.
Human → AI → Human: make your own observation or calculation, ask AI to explain or critique it using supplied evidence, then compare its response with your actual files and design.
Next: Set up the workspace
crumbs: 1  AI-Assisted RNA-Seq Analysis with R

title: Required setup
text:
1. Download and open the complete project
R performs the analysis; Quarto displays the lessons and renders your report. Complete setup once, then follow the examples in order.
Open the RNA-seq repository, choose Code → Download ZIP, and extract the download. In VS Code, choose File → Open Folder and select the inner folder containing _quarto.yml, data/, scripts/ and examples/. Its name may end in -main; no renaming is required. Do not work inside a compressed ZIP.
The learner distribution should also include renv.lock, .Rprofile and renv/activate.R. Activation files may be hidden in the file browser. Choose Terminal → New Terminal. This is the main project folder; guide terminal commands run here unless told to enter reports/.

title: Required setup
text:
2. Check the tools and prompts
Install R and Quarto. An editor such as VS Code or RStudio is useful. Reopen the terminal after installation and check:
Rscript --version
quarto --version
Use the R version recorded in the supplied lockfile. renv restores packages; it does not install R itself. On Windows, these same commands belong in PowerShell; on macOS/Linux, use the terminal shell.






Terminal versus R console



Rscript and quarto commands belong in the terminal. Code labelled R belongs in an R console started from the project folder. If you see an R > prompt, use q(save = "no") before entering terminal commands. Do not copy prompt symbols or use Ctrl+Z as a substitute for exiting R.

title: Required setup
text:
3. Restore the project environment
Rscript scripts/R/setup.R
Wait for Setup complete. The first restore needs internet access and can take time. The helper restores the supplied package versions, confirms that DESeq2, ggplot2, airway and SummarizedExperiment load, and checks project synchronization. It does not install arbitrary current releases or create a learner lockfile.
If the lockfile or activation files are missing, stop and obtain the complete tested environment. Environment initialization belongs to the maintainer; see the appendix. Do not generate a new lockfile to silence a failed installation.

title: Required setup
text:
4. Check the synthetic inputs
Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/synthetic results/synthetic --check-only
Expect 12 samples, 2,000 genes and design ~ donor + group. Check-only validates inputs/design structure but does not fit DESeq2 or refresh figures. If synthetic inputs are absent, run Rscript scripts/R/prepare_synthetic.R first.
Continue with Define: Synthetic practice. That path explains the full run and the independent A01 verification before asking you to interpret results.

title: Required setup
text:
5. Preview and return later
quarto preview
Press Ctrl+C to stop preview. quarto render builds the complete book. Rendering does not run analysis; saved preview images must exist or be generated with the example’s workflow command.
For another session, reopen this same project folder. .Rprofile activates its environment. If packages or the library have changed, run setup to restore the recorded state before analysing again. Inputs go in data/DATASET/, figures/tables in results/DATASET/ and learner writing in ignored reports/.
Next: Start synthetic practice

title: One workflow for every dataset
text:
Use the output map
Use the same seven steps with synthetic practice, airway data and your own study. Keep the original example filenames; their titles identify the learning step.
Replace DATASET with synthetic, airway or my-study. Figures and TSV tables belong in results/DATASET/figures/ and results/DATASET/tables/ respectively.
The six PNGs are library-sizes.png, sample-pca.png, sample-distances.png, ma-plot.png, volcano.png and selected-gene.png.

crumbs: 3  One workflow for every dataset

title: One workflow for every dataset
text:
Keep three distinctions visible
Validation is not design review. A readable matrix and full-rank formula cannot establish biological independence or accurate metadata.
Exploration is not the fitted test. PCA and distances use transformed expression; DESeq2 inference uses raw counts with model-based normalization and dispersion. A visually separated group is not the statistical test of differential expression.
Verification has a scope. The sample verifier checks two raw summaries. A raw-count/size-factor check explains a normalized display. Neither reconstructs all fitted coefficients or adjusted p-values. The script saves hashes but the sample verifier does not automatically validate them.
Use AI after making your own observation: supply the relevant values, ask it to critique the interpretation, then check its response against files and design. Do not send private participant data or let AI invent metadata or results.
Changing inputs, scripts or model choices requires a complete rerun and new checks before interpreting results. A report’s prose does not update automatically.
crumbs: 3  One workflow for every dataset

title: One workflow for every dataset
text:
Count the result sets explicitly
In an R console opened from the main folder, set the dataset name for the run you are reviewing:
dataset <- "synthetic"  # use "airway" or "my-study" for another run
result <- read.delim(file.path("results", dataset, "tables", "differential-expression.tsv"))
cat("Retained result rows:", nrow(result), "\n")
cat("Available p-values:", sum(!is.na(result$pvalue)), "\n")
cat("Available adjusted p-values:", sum(!is.na(result$padj)), "\n")
cat("padj < 0.05:", sum(result$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
The run log’s genes_tested label records the number of retained result rows; not every row necessarily has an available p-value. Keep these counts separate in a report. Exit R with q(save = "no") before entering terminal commands.
crumbs: 3  One workflow for every dataset

title: Write the report
text:
1. Create a starter
A report should let another reader identify the question, follow the contrast, trace a key number and understand the strongest supported conclusion. A collection of six plots is not yet that account.
From the main project folder:
Use airway or my-study for the other paths. The helper creates reports/synthetic-report.qmd and a separate Quarto configuration inside reports/. It preserves an existing report. The tracked starter is templates/report.qmd; generated learner writing and HTML remain ignored.

title: Write the report
text: Rscript scripts/R/create_report.R synthetic

title: Write the report
text:
2. Write from the evidence







Section
What a reader needs




Question/design
Numerator, reference, biological units and any pairing


Data/methods
Source, preprocessing boundary, count units, filter, model and versions


Results
Raw sample summary, retained gene count, fitted estimates and six figure observations


Verification
Exact sample/gene IDs, manual values, saved values and verdicts


Interpretation
Supported conclusions, alternatives and design/technical limits


AI use
Assistance received and checks you performed


Reproduce/next step
Exact commands and one justified follow-up



Use the saved run log for model/contrast and the output map to locate each number. State the denominator when counting genes meeting a threshold: input genes, retained result rows and genes with available adjusted p-values are different sets.
For a reported gene, give the direction and magnitude of the effect, uncertainty and adjusted evidence. Do not translate padj into the probability that the gene is unchanged. Explain missing values rather than treating them as zero or as discoveries.
A normalized-count check uses the saved size factors; a raw-summary check verifies only its stated quantities. Describe those limits so “verified” is not mistaken for independent confirmation of the entire fitted analysis.

title: Write the report
text:
3. Render separately from the book
After completing the analysis and editing the report:
cd reports
quarto render synthetic-report.qmd
cd ..
Replace the report name for the other datasets. The HTML stays in reports/ and embeds the six figures for convenient sharing. Inspect it for missing images, bracketed starter text, incorrect contrasts and private data before sharing.
Keep reports out of _quarto.yml. The helper will not rewrite a report you created earlier; update older image paths and the separate report configuration manually if needed.
Final learner check: can a reader reconstruct one raw-count check, identify the fitted comparison and tell an observation from a proposed biological explanation?

title: Define: Synthetic practice
text:
The question
Which fictional genes show a model-estimated difference in B relative to A, after accounting for paired donor differences?
This is a paired bulk RNA-seq simulation: 2,000 genes, 12 samples and six fictional donors. Each donor contributes one A sample and one B sample. An A/B pair belongs together; the 12 columns do not represent 12 independent donors.
The model is ~ donor + group. The donor term accounts for systematic baseline differences across donors. The contrast is group B A: positive log2 fold change means higher model-estimated expression in B relative to A.
The generator deliberately varies baseline expression, count depth, dispersion, donor effects and donor-specific response. Most genes have no simulated condition effect. Twenty have a zero generating mean. The simulation includes two prespecified expression examples as well as a gene selected after fitting.

title: Define: Synthetic practice
text:
What you will learn
You will match sample IDs, inspect pairing, run the count-model workflow, interpret six figures, independently check one raw-count summary and trace plotted normalized counts to size factors. The final report will connect a result to its contrast and limits.
These are fictional measurements. A small adjusted p-value is evidence within the fitted simulation model, not a biological discovery. Known generating effects are useful for discussing the workflow but are not the same quantity as noisy fitted estimates.

title: Define: Synthetic practice
text:
Your task
Write the question in your own words. Identify the six pairs and complete:

A positive log2 fold change means higher expression in … relative to …, accounting for … .

Then state one conclusion that a simulation cannot support about an organism or treatment.
Optional AI prompt: “Review my interpretation of this paired A/B question and contrast. Keep simulated labels fictional and identify what the donor term does.”
Before moving on: you can name the numerator, reference and pairing unit without looking at the plot.
Next: Preview the results

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Library sizes
Start by exploring the prepared results from the fictional paired experiment. If the prepared project results are present, you can view them before running analysis. Later, you will check the inputs, reproduce the same figures and verify selected numbers.
The project’s saved preview figures and supporting tables belong in results/synthetic/. These results are generated by scripts/R/run_workflow.R, which is also used for your practice run. Quarto displays the saved images; rendering does not fit DESeq2.
Comparison direction: positive log2 fold changes mean higher expression in B relative to A. Check this against run-log.txt before interpreting a gene.
Each bar sums the supplied raw gene counts for one sample. Unequal totals motivate normalization; they do not describe overall FASTQ or alignment quality.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text: Library sizes for the fictional paired experiment.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
PCA



PCA for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a sample; colour shows condition and shape shows donor or cell line. Grey lines connect paired samples. Axis labels give the variation explained. PCA uses up to 500 most variable genes after variance stabilization. Donor variation remains visible: including donor in the fitted model does not remove it from these transformed counts.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Sample-distance heatmap



Sample-distance heatmap for the fictional paired experiment.


Each tile is a Euclidean distance between two samples, using all retained variance-stabilized genes. Darker tiles indicate larger distances. Rows and columns follow hierarchical clustering; diagonal distances are zero. The two annotation strips identify donor and condition. In this bundled simulation, donor pairs sit next to each other in the clustered order: donor variation remains important even with a condition effect. Compare both treatment and donor labels.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
MA plot



MA plot for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a retained gene with a finite fold-change estimate. The horizontal axis is the mean normalized count on a log scale; the vertical axis is the unshrunken log2 fold change. Colours distinguish adjusted p-values below 0.05, other available values and unavailable values. Low-count estimates may be unstable.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Volcano plot



Volcano plot for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point has a finite fold-change estimate and an available adjusted p-value. The vertical axis is -log10(adjusted p-value), so higher points have smaller adjusted p-values. The dashed horizontal line marks 0.05. Missing adjusted p-values are omitted; numerical zeros are floored for display. The plot uses unshrunken effects and does not impose an effect-size cutoff.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Selected-gene expression



Selected-gene expression for the fictional paired experiment.


Each point is a DESeq2 normalized count; lines connect the same donor or cell line across conditions. The three panels show the gene with the lowest available adjusted p-value, a prespecified gene with no simulated condition effect, and a prespecified gene with variable donor response. The latter two were chosen before fitting, using plot-examples.tsv. “No simulated effect” describes the generating parameter; its observed counts and fitted effect can still differ between conditions. Each panel has its own vertical scale. The first gene is selected after analysis and is illustrative. Normalized counts adjust for size factors; they do not remove donor effects or independently validate the model.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
section: Reference values to check against your run
text:
Reference values to check against your run
The supplied reference input has 2,000 fictional genes and 12 samples from six paired donors. A01 has 629,417 supplied counts and 1935 detected genes. After filtering, 1,839 genes are retained in the DE result. Compare input gene count, detected genes for one sample, retained genes and genes with available adjusted p-values: they are different quantities.
PC1 explains 19.4% and PC2 16.7% of variation among the 500 genes used for PCA. The retained genes used for the distance heatmap are a larger set, so the two displays need not emphasize identical patterns.
The post-analysis selected gene is Gene_1515, with estimated log2 fold change 2.391 and adjusted p-value 1.6e-31, for B relative to A while accounting for donor. Its large, consistent change is only one example. Compare it with Gene_0002 (no simulated condition effect) and Gene_0003 (variable donor response), whose panels use separate vertical scales.
These values identify the bundled run; report these fitted values only after checking your own tables. Inputs, software or method changes can change them. All labels and generating effects are fictional.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Check your understanding

Which samples are paired, and where can you see those pairs?
Does a PCA separation identify statistically significant genes?
Which direction does a positive log2 fold change represent?
Why might a large fold change have weak statistical evidence?
Why is a selected-gene plot not an independent confirmation of its adjusted p-value?

All gene labels and effects here are fictional. Do not assign real biological mechanisms to them.

title: Preview: Synthetic practice
text:
Your evidence note
For each figure, record one observation, the supporting table or axis and one limit. A figure selected or generated from the fitted result is a display of that analysis, not an independent experiment. Missing images mean the saved outputs need to be generated; Quarto does not fit DESeq2 while rendering.
Next: Meet the data

title: Meet: Synthetic practice
text:
Prepare or inspect the inputs
For the first reproduction, keep the supplied inputs unchanged. If they are missing or you deliberately want to recreate the revised simulation, run from the main project folder:
The current generator uses seed 20261126 and overwrites only the synthetic input files. Recreate results afterward; old outputs do not automatically become valid for new inputs.
Samples are columns in counts and rows in metadata. A01 and B01 share D01; the equivalent suffix pairing continues through D06. Count zeros are valid observed zeros. A missing value means unavailable information and is rejected by this workflow.

title: Meet: Synthetic practice
text:
Rscript scripts/R/prepare_synthetic.R








File in data/synthetic/
What it contains




gene-counts.tsv
2,000 gene rows; first column gene_id; sample columns A01–A06 and B01–B06


sample-metadata.tsv
12 sample rows; first column sample_id, then group and donor


simulation-truth.tsv
Generating expression, dispersion and donor-specific effects


simulation-samples.tsv
Library multipliers used during simulation


plot-examples.tsv
Prespecified Gene_0002 and Gene_0003 expression examples


simulation-record.txt
Version, seed and construction rules

title: Meet: Synthetic practice
text:
Inspect in R
Open an R console from the main project folder:
counts <- read.delim("data/synthetic/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
metadata <- read.delim("data/synthetic/sample-metadata.tsv")
cat("genes:", nrow(counts), "samples:", ncol(counts) - 1, "\n")
print(table(metadata$donor, metadata$group))
print(head(counts[, 1:4]))
Exit with q(save = "no") before using terminal commands again. Each donor/group table entry should be one.

title: Meet: Synthetic practice
section: Do not confuse construction with estimation
text:
Do not confuse construction with estimation
A generating effect of zero does not force identical observed A/B counts. Library multipliers are not DESeq2’s estimated size factors. plot-examples.tsv influences the teaching panels, not the fitted model. Counts, estimated effects and statistical evidence must still be inspected.
Your task: trace A01 and B01 across both main tables. Locate Gene_0002 and Gene_0003 in the truth and plotting files, and explain why their observed estimates need not equal their generating parameters exactly.
Next: Check the inputs

title: Check: Synthetic practice
text:
Validate the files and design
Expect 12 samples, 2,000 genes and design ~ donor + group. Check-only stops before package-dependent fitting and does not refresh results.
The script checks first-column names, duplicate or missing identifiers, matching sample sets, finite nonnegative integer counts and nonzero sample totals. It reorders metadata rows to count-column order. It also rejects missing values anywhere in the supplied metadata, including extra columns.
For this paired layout, group must contain A and B, and each donor must have exactly one sample in each group. The model matrix must have full rank and residual degrees of freedom. These checks detect some unsupported layouts; they do not establish biological independence or a good study design.

title: Check: Synthetic practice
text: Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/synthetic results/synthetic --check-only

title: Check: Synthetic practice
text:
Inspect the pairing yourself
Open sample-metadata.tsv. Confirm six distinct donors, six A samples and six B samples, with A01/B01 assigned to D01 and the other pairs following the same rule. Do not infer pairing solely from column position.
The gene filter is applied later: a gene must have at least 10 counts in at least two samples, across the whole matrix. It is not a requirement of 10 counts in each condition or every donor. Structural input validation and expression filtering are different steps.

title: Check: Synthetic practice
text:
Your task
Record the dimensions, pairing rule, design and contrast. Explain why 12 samples here provide six complete pairs, not 12 independent donors. Predict what happens if B01 is absent: the existing paired template should stop, not silently treat the study as complete.
Optional AI prompt: “Review this metadata summary and model formula. Identify what is checked automatically and what still depends on knowing how samples were generated.”
Before moving on: the check passes and the A/B contrast is scientifically meaningful within the simulation.
Next: Run the analysis

title: Run: Synthetic practice
text:
Reproduce the outputs
Run from the main project folder and stop if an error occurs. Named outputs are overwritten on rerun; an interrupted run can leave a mixture of older and newer files. Interpret only a completed run.

title: Run: Synthetic practice
text: Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/synthetic results/synthetic

title: Run: Synthetic practice
text:
Follow the three numerical representations







Representation
Where it is used




Raw integer counts
Input summaries and the DESeq2 count model


Counts divided by estimated size factors
Normalized-count tables and gene-expression panels


Variance-stabilized retained counts
PCA and sample distances



DESeq2 estimates size factors and dispersions while fitting ~ donor + group; it does not test the variance-stabilized matrix. Normalized counts are not counts per million or the single-cell guide’s counts per 10,000.
The filter keeps genes with counts ≥10 in at least two samples. The supplied reference run retained 1,839 of 2,000 genes. Confirm your own result-row count. The raw sample-QC table uses all input genes, so a sample’s detected-gene count can exceed the number of retained genes.
results() uses contrast B versus A and alpha = 0.05. The table includes unshrunken log2 fold changes, standard errors, p-values and adjusted p-values. Plot colour uses padj < 0.05; there is no minimum effect-size rule. A missing adjusted p-value is not a discovery or a numerical zero.

title: Run: Synthetic practice
text:
Understand the visualizations
PCA uses up to 500 most variable variance-stabilized genes. The distance heatmap uses all retained transformed genes. The transformation uses blind = FALSE, but does not subtract donor effects. Modelling donor in differential expression is not the same as removing donor structure from PCA.
The selected-gene display supplements a post-analysis choice with Gene_0002 and Gene_0003, fixed in the simulation before fitting. Panels have separate y-scales; compare numbers rather than steepness across panels.

title: Run: Synthetic practice
text:
Your task
Read results/synthetic/run-log.txt and confirm group B A, the filter and retained gene count. Locate the corresponding figure tables using the output map. Record input, retained and available-adjusted-p-value gene counts separately.
Before moving on: all six figures exist and each interpretation can be traced to the current run.
Next: Verify and explain

title: Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice
text:
Check A01 independently
For the current simulation, expect 629,417 supplied counts and 1,935 detected genes. The independent script reads the raw column and saved sample-QC row and compares those two quantities. It does not rerun or validate the DESeq2 fit, adjusted p-values or every input/script hash.
Repeat the arithmetic in an R console opened in the main project folder:
Exit with q(save = "no") before using terminal commands again. Do not edit a saved value to force agreement; investigate the input version and completed run first.

x <- read.delim("data/synthetic/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
qc <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/sample-qc.tsv")
sum(x$A01)

crumbs: 10  Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice

title: Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice
text:
Trace the normalized gene display
In an R console:
raw <- read.delim("data/synthetic/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
size <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/size-factors.tsv")
gene <- read.delim("results/synthetic/tables/selected-gene-counts.tsv")
i <- match(gene$gene_id[1], raw$gene_id)
v <- as.numeric(unlist(raw[i, gene$sample_id], use.names = FALSE))
sf <- size$size_factor[match(gene$sample_id, size$sample_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(v), !anyNA(sf), all(sf > 0))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v / sf, gene$normalized_count, tolerance = 1e-8)))
print(gene)
This checks plotted normalized counts against raw counts and saved size factors. It does not independently estimate those factors or reproduce a fitted coefficient. A raw A/B ratio, a normalized-count ratio and the model’s donor-adjusted effect are different calculations.
crumbs: 10  Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice

title: Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice
text:
Inspect a fitted result
Open tables/differential-expression.tsv inside results/synthetic/. Select a row and record gene_id, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and padj. Confirm its sign against group B A in the run log. Count missing adjusted p-values separately; their absence can arise from independent filtering or outlier handling, among other reasons.
Compare Gene_0002 and Gene_0003 with simulation-truth.tsv and tables/example-gene-counts.tsv. No generating condition effect does not guarantee a fitted effect of exactly zero. Variable donor responses need not all point in the same direction. Keep both examples rather than selecting only an attractive result.
crumbs: 10  Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice

title: Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice
text:
Explain six figures with evidence
Write one sentence per figure, using a raw total, PCA percentage, sample distance or gene estimate from its table. A small adjusted p-value concerns the fitted test; it does not make the gene biologically important. The post-analysis selected-gene plot reuses the fitted dataset and is not independent confirmation.
Your task: keep a record of A01’s manual/saved values, one normalized-count check, one correctly directed gene estimate and one limitation. Check provenance in tables/input-script-hashes.tsv yourself if input or script versions are uncertain; this verifier does not automatically enforce it.
Next: Write the report
crumbs: 10  Verify and Explain: Synthetic practice

title: Write: Synthetic practice
text:
Create your report
Open reports/synthetic-report.qmd. The helper creates a separate Quarto project inside ignored reports/ and preserves existing writing. The tracked starter lives in templates/report.qmd. Follow Write the report for the shared structure.

title: Write: Synthetic practice
text: Rscript scripts/R/create_report.R synthetic

title: Write: Synthetic practice
text:
Turn the checks into evidence
Use the real values from your run. A checked raw-summary sentence is:

The fictional input contained 2,000 genes and 12 samples from six paired donors. A01’s 629,417 supplied counts and 1,935 detected genes were independently verified. The differential comparison was B relative to A, accounting for donor.

Add the retained gene count, one fitted effect with uncertainty/adjusted evidence, a normalized-count check and observations from all six figures. Keep generating parameters separate from estimates. Do not assign real biological functions to fictional gene IDs.

title: Write: Synthetic practice
text:
Render and review
From the main project folder:
cd reports
quarto render synthetic-report.qmd
cd ..
Read reports/synthetic-report.html. The starter links all six figures in ../results/synthetic/figures/ and embeds them in the rendered HTML. Confirm they display, remove bracketed starter text and trace every number to a table or calculation. Existing older reports are not rewritten automatically; update their image paths and rendering configuration as needed.
Your task: identify one statement supported by an independent calculation, one by the fitted model, and one describing a limitation. State how AI helped and what you checked yourself.
Keep generated reports and HTML in ignored reports/, separate from book chapters. Inspect content for private data before sharing.

title: Define: Airway case study
text:
The question
Which genes differ in dexamethasone-treated versus untreated airway smooth-muscle cell-line samples, accounting for baseline differences among cell lines?
This real dataset comes from Himes et al. (2014), available through the Bioconductor airway package. The packaged experiment has eight samples from four cell lines, each measured untreated and treated. This is bulk RNA-seq: each count column describes a sample, not one single cell.
The model is ~ cell + dex. cell identifies the matched cell line; dex identifies treatment. The contrast is dex trt untrt: positive log2 fold changes mean higher model-estimated expression in treated samples relative to untreated samples, accounting for cell line.
The input matrix is downstream of count generation. This practical does not process FASTQ reads, assess alignment quality or reproduce every analysis in the original publication.

title: Define: Airway case study
text:
Set the interpretation boundary
The paired design supports studying the treatment contrast in these measured cell lines under the fitted model. It does not by itself demonstrate clinical benefit, establish every gene’s mechanism or justify generalization to all airway cell populations.
Including cell line in the model accommodates baseline differences; it does not erase those differences from normalized counts or PCA. You will inspect treatment and cell-line structure together.

title: Define: Airway case study
text:
Your task
Write the question and identify the numerator, reference and pairing variable. State why the eight samples are four matched pairs rather than eight unrelated biological sources. Name one conclusion that requires evidence beyond this count-matrix analysis.
Optional AI prompt: “Review my description of this paired treatment comparison. Distinguish what the experiment measures from a clinical or mechanistic claim.”
Before moving on: the treatment contrast and the role of cell line are explicit.
Next: Preview the results

title: Preview: Airway case study
text:
Library sizes
Start by exploring the prepared results from the real airway experiment. If the prepared project results are present, you can view them before running analysis. Later, you will check the inputs, reproduce the same figures and verify selected numbers.
The project’s saved preview figures and supporting tables belong in results/airway/. These results are generated by scripts/R/run_workflow.R, which is also used for your practice run. Quarto displays the saved images; rendering does not fit DESeq2.
Comparison direction: positive log2 fold changes mean higher expression in trt relative to untrt, accounting for cell line. Check this against run-log.txt before interpreting a gene.
Each bar sums the supplied raw gene counts for one sample. Unequal totals motivate normalization; they do not describe overall FASTQ or alignment quality.

PCA



PCA for the real airway experiment.


Each point is a sample; colour shows condition and shape shows donor or cell line. Grey lines connect paired samples. Axis labels give the variation explained. PCA uses up to 500 most variable genes after variance stabilization. Donor variation remains visible: including donor in the fitted model does not remove it from these transformed counts.

title: Preview: Airway case study
text:
Sample-distance heatmap



Sample-distance heatmap for the real airway experiment.


Each tile is a Euclidean distance between two samples, using all retained variance-stabilized genes. Darker tiles indicate larger distances. Rows and columns follow hierarchical clustering; diagonal distances are zero. Compare both treatment and donor labels.

title: Preview: Airway case study
text:
MA plot



MA plot for the real airway experiment.


Each point is a retained gene with a finite fold-change estimate. The horizontal axis is the mean normalized count on a log scale; the vertical axis is the unshrunken log2 fold change. Colours distinguish adjusted p-values below 0.05, other available values and unavailable values. Low-count estimates may be unstable.

title: Preview: Airway case study
text:
Volcano plot



Volcano plot for the real airway experiment.


Each point has a finite fold-change estimate and an available adjusted p-value. The vertical axis is -log10(adjusted p-value), so higher points have smaller adjusted p-values. The dashed horizontal line marks 0.05. Missing adjusted p-values are omitted; numerical zeros are floored for display. The plot uses unshrunken effects and does not impose an effect-size cutoff.

title: Preview: Airway case study
text:
Selected-gene expression



Selected-gene expression for the real airway experiment.


Each point is a DESeq2 normalized count; lines connect the same donor or cell line across conditions. The title names the gene with the lowest available adjusted p-value (ties follow the saved result order); if none is available, the highest mean normalized count is used. Selection happens after analysis and is illustrative. Normalized counts adjust for size factors; they do not remove donor effects or independently validate the model.

title: Preview: Airway case study
section: Reference values to check against your run
text:
Reference values to check against your run
The supplied reference run has 8 samples. Its first sample, SRR1039508, has 20,637,971 supplied counts and 24633 detected genes. PC1 explains 47.7% and PC2 23.5% of the variation used for PCA.
The selected-gene figure shows ENSG00000152583, with an estimated log2 fold change of 4.574 and adjusted p-value 7.32e-132 for trt versus untrt, accounting for cell line. Trace these values to the tables when you reach verification. These are reference values reported in the supplied guide; use your own recorded outputs after rerunning or changing inputs.

Which samples are paired, and where can you see those pairs?
Does a PCA separation identify statistically significant genes?
Which direction does a positive log2 fold change represent?
Why might a large fold change have weak statistical evidence?
Why is a selected-gene plot not an independent confirmation of its adjusted p-value?

Airway gene identifiers refer to the supplied annotation. Gene names, functions and mechanisms require a documented annotation source and supporting evidence.

title: Meet: Airway case study
text:
Export the packaged count matrix
From the main project folder:
The script loads the airway data object from the installed package and writes the original assay and selected sample metadata as TSVs. It does not download sequencing reads or use a transcript-level normalized table. Rerunning exports the files again, so regenerate results afterward.
The cell values identify the four cell lines. dex contains untrt and trt. Each cell line contributes one sample in each condition. Sample identifiers such as SRR1039508 are labels to match across files; they are not condition names.

Inspect the matching and pairs
This is R-console code:
counts <- read.delim("data/airway/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
metadata <- read.delim("data/airway/sample-metadata.tsv")

Preserve the meaning of identifiers
Rows use the identifiers supplied by the package. A gene ID is not automatically a gene symbol, function or pathway. The selected-gene example can be checked numerically without attaching a mechanistic name to it. Functional interpretation requires a documented annotation source and further evidence.
Record the package version and original citation in your report: Himes et al. (2014), DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0099625. Keep the sample-level source and pairing information with the data.

title: Check: Airway case study
text:
Run the structural and design check
After exporting the inputs:
Expect eight samples and design ~ cell + dex. Record the reported number of genes. Check-only validates the inputs and model structure; it does not fit DESeq2 or replace earlier tables and figures.
The checker verifies identifiers, matching sample sets, integer nonnegative counts, nonzero sample totals and missing values. It aligns metadata to the count-column order. For this layout, dex must contain untrt and trt, and each cell line must appear exactly once in each condition.
It also checks that the model matrix is full rank and has residual degrees of freedom. This detects certain confounded or saturated designs, but cannot prove that the metadata labels or biological replication are correct.

title: Check: Airway case study
text: Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/airway results/airway --check-only

title: Check: Airway case study
text:
Review the pairing yourself
Open the metadata and make a cell-line-by-condition table. Every entry should equal one. Check one named pair in the source records. Removing a troublesome sample would break its complete pair in this template; investigate and document the design implications rather than removing it silently.
The prefilter applied during Run is counts ≥10 in at least two samples, across all samples. It removes low-information genes before fitting. It is not a sample-exclusion rule or a guarantee that every retained gene receives an adjusted p-value.

title: Check: Airway case study
text:
Your task
Record the dimensions, four complete pairs, formula and contrast dex trt untrt. Explain what passing the rank check establishes and what still depends on reliable experimental metadata.
Optional AI prompt: “Review this paired metadata table and intended model. Flag a possible mismatch or confounding issue without inventing missing samples.”
Before moving on: the check passes and you can explain why the cell-line term belongs in this analysis.
Next: Run the analysis

title: Run: Airway case study
text:
Fit the documented comparison
The workflow repeats input checks, records raw sample summaries, filters genes and fits DESeq2 using ~ cell + dex. It requests treated versus untreated, with alpha = 0.05. Verify dex trt untrt in results/airway/run-log.txt before interpreting effect direction.
Named outputs are replaced on rerun. If fitting or plotting fails, stop before using the output folder: some files may be from an earlier run.

title: Run: Airway case study
text: Rscript scripts/R/run_workflow.R data/airway results/airway

title: Run: Airway case study
text:
Keep modelling and visualization distinct
DESeq2 fits raw integer counts using its normalization and dispersion estimates. The saved normalized counts divide retained counts by estimated size factors. They do not remove cell-line effects.
The script also applies varianceStabilizingTransformation(..., blind = FALSE) for exploration. Those transformed values feed PCA and distances, not the differential-expression test. blind = FALSE does not subtract the cell-line term or make the data batch-corrected.
PCA uses up to 500 most variable transformed genes. The sample-distance heatmap uses all retained transformed genes, so the figures need not emphasize identical relationships. Grey PCA lines identify paired samples, not trajectories or a significance test.

title: Run: Airway case study
text:
Read estimates with uncertainty
tables/differential-expression.tsv includes the unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and padj. Positive means higher in treated samples. A log2 fold change of 1 corresponds to a model-estimated twofold change; −1 corresponds to half, in the stated contrast.
MA and volcano colours use padj < 0.05, without an effect-size cutoff. An unavailable adjusted p-value must be investigated, not counted as a discovery. The selected-gene plot generally shows the lowest available adjusted p-value, chosen after fitting. If none is available, the script falls back to a high-mean gene; check the run and table rather than assuming it is statistically selected.

title: Verify and Explain: Airway case study
text:
Verify the normalized-count display
In an R console:
raw <- read.delim("data/airway/gene-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
size <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/size-factors.tsv")
gene <- read.delim("results/airway/tables/selected-gene-counts.tsv")
i <- match(gene$gene_id[1], raw$gene_id)
v <- as.numeric(unlist(raw[i, gene$sample_id], use.names = FALSE))
sf <- size$size_factor[match(gene$sample_id, size$sample_id)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(v), !anyNA(sf), all(sf > 0))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(v / sf, gene$normalized_count, tolerance = 1e-8)))
print(gene)
Exit R before entering terminal commands again. Agreement checks the saved display against raw counts and saved factors; it does not independently estimate factors, dispersions, fold changes or adjusted p-values.

title: Define: Your own study
text:
Write the comparison before running code
State one question about gene-level counts across two conditions. Identify the organism, tissue, biological source, sample collection and how counts were generated. Decide which condition is the numerator and which is the reference.
A useful planning sentence is:
A sample is a measurement unit; a donor or experimental source may contribute several samples. Technical replicates, matched repeated samples and independent biological replicates play different roles. Do not infer independence merely from different column names.

title: Define: Your own study
text: I will compare [numerator] with [reference] in [sample population], accounting for [supported pairing/design terms].

title: Define: Your own study
section: Check that this template matches your study
text:
Check that this template matches your study
The supplied script supports two-condition A/B comparisons, with or without complete donor pairs, and the specific paired airway-style cell/dex layout. It does not automatically choose a model for arbitrary condition names, time courses, incomplete pairs, nested factors or interactions.
If the study requires another design, pause for an explicit, reviewed adaptation of the script. Adding a batch column does not make the current model adjust for batch. Renaming conditions to pass a checker does not solve confounding or missing replication.

title: Define: Your own study
text:
Your task
Write a short analysis brief:

The biological question and count source.
The true independent sources and any pairing.
The numerator, reference and intended model terms.
Potential confounding and missing design information.
One conclusion this analysis cannot establish.

If you deliberately encode real conditions as A/B, retain a documented mapping to their original names and verify the contrast throughout the report. Do not hide the original meanings or treat encoding as validation of the design.
Optional AI prompt: “Review my question, design and metadata summary. Identify unsupported assumptions and whether this existing script matches the study; do not invent replicates or covariates.”
Before moving on: you can justify the comparison independently of whether it produces significant genes.
Next: Preview the outputs

title: Preview: Your own study
text:
Know what the outputs can answer
Your figures appear only after you supply inputs and complete analysis. The goal is a checked result, not a desired number of significant genes or clean condition separation.
Corresponding numbers belong in results/my-study/tables/. Read the output map before drafting claims.

Figure inside results/my-study/figures/
Question to ask

title: Preview: Your own study
text:
Anticipate different valid outcomes
PCA may emphasize donor variation, batch effects, condition or another source. Overlap does not mean there are no differentially expressed genes. Separation does not identify which genes are statistically supported. The design terms used in fitting are not automatically removed from transformed or normalized data.
The workflow colours gene points using padj < 0.05, without requiring a minimum effect size. It plots unshrunken effects, omits missing adjusted p-values from the volcano and selects an illustrative gene after analysis. These displays do not independently validate the test.
No gene meeting the decision threshold is also a reportable result. Examine sample size, uncertainty, design and data quality; do not keep modifying a model until a desired result appears.

title: Preview: Your own study
text:
Your task
Write two plausible outcomes, including one without clear separation or discoveries. For each, name an output you would inspect and evidence needed to interpret it. Choose a statement that can be checked numerically and another requiring additional biological evidence.
Before moving on: you can explain what each plot displays without knowing what your study’s result will be.

title: Meet: Your own study
text:
Preserve provenance
Record source, organism, count-generation method, annotation version, date and any identifier changes. Resolve duplicated gene labels using a documented upstream rule rather than dropping rows arbitrarily. Do not treat technical runs as independent biological replicates.
The current checker rejects missing values anywhere in metadata. Keep the supplied table focused on complete, required analysis variables; preserve fuller source metadata separately. Never fill an unknown donor or condition with an invented value merely to pass checks.
Your task: trace one sample across matrix and metadata, identify its biological source and explain the selected design row. Protect participant identifiers before sharing files or AI prompts.

title: Check: Your own study
text:
Run without fitting
The script reports dimensions and its chosen formula. Compare these with your analysis brief. Do not continue if the selected mode or formula differs from the design you intended.
Checks include required first-column names, unique nonempty IDs, matching sample sets, missing values, finite nonnegative integer counts and nonzero totals. Metadata are reordered to match matrix columns. The design matrix must be full rank with residual degrees of freedom.
For an unpaired A/B layout, the checker requires at least two samples per group; that is a software minimum, not a sample-size recommendation or confirmation of adequate power. For a donor-paired layout, every donor needs exactly one A and one B sample. Other pairing structures are unsupported without adaptation.

section: Check what the code cannot know
text:
Check what the code cannot know
Confirm biological independence, condition assignment, pairing and the possible overlap of batch with condition. Full rank does not prove that a variable is measured correctly or that important confounding is absent. A formula with no batch term does not adjust for batch simply because that column exists.
Do not remove a sample or relabel a donor to make validation succeed. Investigate source records and document exclusions or code adaptations before inference.

title: Check: Your own study

Understand the filter to be applied
During Run, genes need counts ≥10 in at least two samples across the input matrix. This is distinct from structural validation, DESeq2’s independent filtering and sample quality review. Record this prefilter, and justify a code change if your assay requires another approach.

text:
Use the reviewed workflow
Only after your study genuinely matches a supported layout, or a documented adaptation has been reviewed:

text:
Interpret the representations correctly
The model uses raw integer counts with DESeq2 size-factor normalization and dispersion estimation. Saved normalized counts divide by those estimated factors. Variance-stabilized values are for PCA and distances, not the differential test. Neither representation automatically removes donor or batch effects.
The result table reports unshrunken log2 fold changes and their uncertainty. The default results request uses alpha = 0.05; colour indicates padj < 0.05 without an effect-size threshold. The PCA uses up to 500 transformed genes; sample distances use all retained transformed genes.
A selected gene is chosen for illustration after fitting. In your study, the extra simulation examples generally do not exist. Do not invent truth labels or compare plots as independent validation.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Key quantities
A log2 fold change of 1 corresponds to a twofold model-estimated difference; −1 corresponds to half. The sign is meaningless without a named contrast. Effects in this script are unshrunken, so inspect their uncertainty rather than ranking solely by magnitude.
The chosen padj < 0.05 rule targets false-discovery-rate control under the procedure’s assumptions. It does not promise that every called gene is true or biologically important. No minimum effect size is required by this script. The default two-sided test concerns a zero effect, not an explicitly tested minimum fold change.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Term
Meaning in this workflow




Raw count
Supplied gene-level read/fragment count for one sample; not TPM/FPKM


Library total
Sum of a raw matrix column, before gene filtering


Detected genes
Number of genes with raw count greater than zero in one sample


Retained gene
A gene with counts ≥10 in at least two samples, entering the fitted dataset


Size factor
DESeq2’s sample-specific normalization factor; not necessarily the simulated library multiplier


Normalized count
Retained raw count divided by the estimated size factor


VST
Variance-stabilizing transformation for exploration, not differential testing input


Log2 fold change
Fitted effect for numerator relative to reference, accounting for design terms


lfcSE
Standard error of the reported log2 fold-change estimate


baseMean
Mean normalized count across samples in the fitted dataset


padj
Multiple-testing-adjusted p-value; not the probability that a particular null is true

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Missing adjusted p-values
Do not replace NA with zero or count it as a discovery. A retained gene can lack an adjusted p-value because of DESeq2 independent filtering or lack a p-value because of outlier handling. Inspect its raw counts, baseMean, p-value and current DESeq2 documentation. The simple count prefilter and DESeq2 independent filtering are different decisions.
The volcano omits missing adjusted p-values. Its numerical zero p-values are floored only for display; saved result values are not changed by plotting. PCA and the distance heatmap summarize transformed sample profiles, not gene-level test significance.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Model and input troubleshooting







Symptom
What to inspect




Missing file
Main project folder and exact relative path


IDs differ
Count columns versus metadata sample_id values, including case


Noninteger counts
Wrong assay, normalized input, text or missing values


Missing metadata
Required variables and extra columns; the checker rejects any missing value


Incomplete pairs
One sample per donor/condition is required by the paired template


Wrong mode/formula
cell/dex takes priority over group; unsupported covariates are not inferred


Rank/degree-of-freedom error
Confounding, saturated design or insufficient replication


Normalized display disagrees
Match samples by ID, use saved size factors and confirm the completed run


Raw verification passes but fitted outputs look old
The verifier checks only two raw summaries; inspect run logs/hashes and rerun fully


Missing report image
Run the dataset workflow and use ../results/DATASET/figures/ from reports/



Changing an input, formula or contrast requires a full rerun and new verification. The script records hashes but the sample verifier does not compare them automatically. An interrupted run may leave earlier outputs, so do not interpret a partially refreshed directory.

title: Appendix A — Appendix
text:
Installation and environment troubleshooting
Use the R version recorded in the supplied lockfile. renv restores packages, not R or system compilation tools. Run Rscript scripts/R/setup.R from the main project folder; do not snapshot an incomplete installation.
If an R console can load a package but the terminal cannot, check .Rprofile, renv/activate.R, the working folder and terminal R executable. In the terminal:
Rscript -e 'cat("DESeq2 available:", requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE), "\n"); print(.libPaths())'
For an inconsistent environment, inspect Rscript -e 'renv::status()'. Keep the first download/compiler error when seeking help; the final dependent-package error may only be a consequence. Missing source compilers or system libraries need the remedy appropriate to that error and operating system, not repeated snapshots or arbitrary repository changes.

Maintainer-only environment creation
Learners should receive an already tested lockfile and activation files. If maintaining a repository that has never been initialized, use a separate maintainer R session in the project folder to initialize an isolated library and install the intended packages:
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("renv")
renv::init(bare = TRUE, restart = FALSE)
renv::settings$snapshot.type("all")
renv::install(c("BiocManager", "ggplot2"))
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "airway", "SummarizedExperiment"),
                     ask = FALSE, update = FALSE)
stopifnot(requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("airway", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE))
This is not a repair recipe for an existing tested environment. Keep that environment and its settings intact. For an initialized project, preserve the recorded package sources and restore rather than silently installing current versions.
After successful synthetic and airway runs, independent checks and report rendering, the maintainer can snapshot the working environment in R:
renv::snapshot(prompt = FALSE)
renv::status()
q(save = "no")
Retain renv.lock, .Rprofile, renv/activate.R, renv/settings.json and renv/.gitignore; exclude the local library. Test restoration in a clean project copy before describing the environment as portable.

Sources and next learning steps

DESeq2 vignette: count modelling, designs, contrasts, transformations and result interpretation.
Airway package and dataset vignette: packaged data and study provenance.
Himes et al. (2014): original airway study.
Bioconductor gene-level RNA-seq workflow: broader worked analysis.
renv introduction: environment creation, recording and restoration.

This guide makes its plotting/filtering choices explicit. It does not implement every optional method in these references. Consider gene annotation, effect-size shrinkage, additional sample QC, an appropriate extended design or functional analysis only when justified by the question and data.
